lens: Adversarial experimental audit of the measured facts only: separate (i) hard constraints that sink a path if ignored, (ii) false comforts (positive-looking results that do not license what they seem to), and (iii) untested assumptions every path silently depends on, then rank (iii) by test cost x path impact. The recurring finding: the target has been characterised well; the learner has never been measured.
principles: P1 [METRIC] Verdicts are decided by a handful of modes (3 of 12,792). The only admissible evidence of progress is eps_op from the full-spectrum evaluator; D/d, e_A, Frobenius, action-MSE are not evidence (D/d misleads by ~100x).

P2 [METRIC][ACCURACY] Error must be multiplicative on a factor, never additive on A: worst-case additive on A needs 4.2e-7 relative (cond 7.2e4), factor error is unamplified (eps_op ~ 1.42||Delta||) but still needs ~1e-4 per entry.

P3 [STRUCTURE] Soft-mode stiffness is a 1e3-1e4 near/far-field cancellation. Any representation that PREDICTS the cancelling terms needs ~1e-5 relative precision on the far field; only representations that COMPUTE the cancellation (assembly of a physics-structured model) have reached near-gate accuracy at low parameter count (collar: 23k params -> 0.15).

P4 [GEOMETRY] The teacher is a stable target at task level (0.023% derivative agreement) and an unstable target at operator level (60% jump in one direction per 1e-4 thickness; 87% derivative disagreement; cross-seat eps_op 536-3847). The contract must match what the teacher defines stably, or the labels must change.

P5 [REPRESENTATIONS] Oracle compressions of a known R* (H-matrix 15% of dense at +-3%) and per-geometry fits with full label information (Newton 0.047, collar 0.15) are upper bounds on what a representation can reach, not evidence of learnability. Learnability additionally requires continuous gauge-free labels, fixed structure across geometries, and a demonstrated one-seat memorisation by a network - none exists.
P6 [LEARNING] Rigid modes must be removed by construction (quotient B); every free parameterisation without it fell into the diagonal-only attractor at exactly 38.8% (10 rounds).

P7 [ASSEMBLY] (inference from Loewner order) eps_op <= eps per cell implies (1-eps)K <= Khat <= (1+eps)K for any lattice assembled from those cells, hence compliance within ~+-eps for every load case - the module gate composes; it does NOT compose to sensitivities (no Loewner bound on derivatives), and the task-level contract has no composition theorem at all.

P8 [GOAL] The cost bar is 31.85 s x 64 cores per cell per geometry. Any inference path that re-assembles fine cut cells and pre-eliminates (collar: ~30 s) or that needs the true operator's action (mode B) must present a cost model against this bar; none exists.

P9 Reachability before training: compute the closed-form oracle floor / Loewner lower bound of any proposed representation before spending optimisation or data on it (this is what killed block-diagonal D and the fixed collar cheaply).

P10 Before generalisation, memorisation: the project has zero neural results below eps_op ~4 on any seat. Architecture and data discussions are premature until one network reproduces one labelled seat to +-10%.
implications_for_representation: Mandatory: (1) factor form on the quotient (A = R^T R with rigid modes removed by construction) [METRIC][LEARNING]; (2) global information flow - no banded, local, or bounded-receptive-field factor can pass (band truncation of the TRUE factor gives eps_op 58 at every radius, ~300 damaged modes; the V1 CNN had receptive radius 0.23 and mu_max 670) [STRUCTURE][LEARNING]; (3) representations with measured reachability floors are dead as-is: block-diagonal D (63-204x above +-10%), multiscale lifting T^T D T (eps_op 15.2 at 7.4M params), banded L + low-rank M (lam_min(H0) 0.02-0.13, no M can pass), fixed one-layer collar (Loewner bound mu_max >= 1.111) [REPRESENTATIONS]; (4) the only structure that passes +-3% needs 11.8-15.6% of dense (>= 1.2e7 numbers per cell), and the gate barely changes that size - the near field dominates storage while the far field decides the verdict; any claim of a much smaller model must first produce an oracle floor [REPRESENTATIONS (a)]; (5) H-matrix coefficients are gauge-non-unique; only block products/actions are valid supervision targets, and fixed ranks per level are untested. Strategic implication (inference): accuracy-per-parameter is best where the operator is COMPUTED from predicted physical quantities (collar+core), so the open representation question is not accuracy but cost - a physics-structured forward map 10-100x cheaper than the teacher whose Loewner reachability bound clears +-10% (e.g. 2-layer collar bound, untested). Whatever is chosen, its per-parameter noise budget must be measured for that parameterisation (1e-3 RMS on the old backend's diagonal moved the spectrum from [0.863,1.114] to [0.707,1.377]).
implications_for_loss_and_metric: (1) The training loss must contain a two-sided worst-direction term in the whitened metric (max |mu-1| or max |log mu|): averaged losses cannot see the deciding modes [METRIC], and the one-sided extreme term tried pushed mu_min from 0.13 to 0.05 while fixing mu_max [LEARNING]. Extreme whitened eigenpairs are cheap by Lanczos with R* actions, so this is affordable per step; it requires R* for every training label (only 33 exist). (2) eps_op from the full-spectrum evaluator is the gate at every checkpoint, on train seats first (memorisation) and held-out second. (3) The Newton dense fit reaching mu in [0.956,1.047] with full information is either a loss ceiling (if plateaued) or unfinished; if it is a ceiling, no network trained through the same loss can beat 5% - resolve before scaling anything. (4) Supervision must be gauge-free (actions/products, not factor coefficients). (5) The gate depends on an undecided contract: module gate (composes to lattice compliance via Loewner, but not to sensitivities) vs task gate (30x looser in mode B, no composition theorem, compliance is first order in general and the 0.31% result is construction-specific). (6) Neither contract has been tested on design sensitivities, which TO needs; the teacher's operator derivative does not exist stably, so any sensitivity contract must be task-level. (7) The metric measures fidelity to the teacher's soft directions, which are GP-dependent by construction (the 60% jump came with 3 new GP faces) and unvalidated against physics; until gamma-sensitivity is measured, +-3% may be a demand to reproduce stabilisation artefacts.
implications_for_data_and_teacher: (1) 33 factored labels, all FULL, sampled sparsely in a geometry space where neighbouring seats differ by eps_op 536-3847 [GEOMETRY]: no held-out claim at +-10% is statistically meaningful from this set, and CUT-through-boundary cells are out of scope until labelled. (2) The label-count bottleneck may be self-imposed: 1024 condensed S packets exist and a dense Cholesky at d ~ 13k is ~7e11 flop (seconds to minutes each) - verify why only 33 have R*; but more labels change nothing until a representation with a learnable target exists. (3) 48-op cube augmentation is exact but only within an orbit; it does not reduce the ~1e3-1e4 whitened-Lipschitz constant of the geometry->operator map. (4) Along any TO path, background-cell activation events (a 5.6e-15 volume fraction cell + 3 GP faces moved one direction 60%) make the module-level label a step function; the density of such events is unmeasured but a single +0.01% perturbation already produced one. Either regenerate labels with a continuous stabilisation (decision 4; must preserve FP64 measurability, the no-GP teacher had cond 4e16), or adopt a task-level contract, or accept that the learner inherits the teacher's non-smoothness into the optimiser. Hard classification cannot fix this (1e-12 threshold flip -> mu_max 1.25). (5) Decision 4 is upstream of all label generation; every label produced before it may need regeneration (tooling exists at the frozen commit). (6) The teacher is validated only at task level (Tet10 compliance 0.05-0.10%); per-direction soft-mode stiffness has never been compared to anything independent, and a GP gamma sweep (1e-3/1e-5) is the cheapest possible check of whether the labels' deciding directions are physics.
implications_for_architecture: (1) Global receptive field is mandatory (cancellation, band failure); a 0.23-radius CNN is disqualified by measurement. (2) Output must live on the quotient by construction and handle variable trace dimension per geometry (d 12,792-15,702 across seats; node masks). (3) Cube-group equivariance or 48x augmentation. (4) The output is either 1e7-1e8 numbers at ~1e-4 relative precision with an unmeasured residual-noise model, or a small set of physical parameters (material tensors, reduced bases) fed to a differentiable assembly that computes the operator; only the second has demonstrated near-gate accuracy per parameter (23k params -> 0.15), but its forward map cost ~30 s, i.e. the teacher's cost, so the architecture problem is inseparable from the cost problem (open decision 3). (5) If the network is fed hard-classified inputs (node mask, support measure) it can represent the teacher's jumps but must learn 60%-per-event sensitivities from rare events; if fed smooth fields it cannot represent them at all - the architecture choice is forced by the label-continuity decision, not the reverse. (6) Optimisation in raw factor coordinates diverges (Adam NaNs); the local-geometry column scaling (R^2 0.98, LOSO curvature spread 1e4 -> 16.8) is a preconditioner that any factor-emitting architecture should bake in - but it is a conditioning result, not a label. (7) No architecture discussion is warranted until a one-seat memorisation to +-10% exists; that experiment also delivers the first real residual-noise model.
hard_constraints: C1 [METRIC] Acceptance is worst-direction only: eps_op = max|mu-1| over the whitened spectrum; 3 of 12,792 modes decided a verdict; D/d = 1.27e-5 cleared the +-3% necessary line by 36x while eps_op = 0.229 failed +-10%. Sinks: any path whose evidence or training signal is an averaged loss (Frobenius, mean divergence, e_A, action-MSE).

C2 [METRIC] Additive error on A is amplified by cond(A) = 7.2e4: worst-case +-3% needs ||E||_2 <= 1.46e-8 (4.2e-7 relative); even structured per-entry error on A needs ~5.5e-5. Sinks: direct regression of S/A with generic residuals.

C3 [METRIC][ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS] Factor error is unamplified (eps_op ~ 1.42||Delta||) but +-3% still needs ~2.7e-4 per entry independent, ~1.2e-4 spatially coherent (111x ~ sqrt(d) amplification), and 1e-3 RMS on a different parameterisation cost 0.14 -> 0.38 eps_op. Sinks: any regression whose demonstrated precision is 1e-2..1e-3 (all so far: V1 at 27% e_A).

C4 [STRUCTURE OF S] Soft stiffness is a 1e3-1e4 near/far-field cancellation; truncating the TRUE factor to radius 0.25 (6% of entries) gives eps_op 58, ~300 damaged modes at every radius, mu_max 59-144. Sinks: banded/local factors, local receptive fields, Frobenius-locality arguments (99.87% energy within 0.05 is irrelevant to the verdict), and any far-field prediction less precise than ~1e-5 relative.
C5 [LEARNING ATTEMPTS] Without rigid invariance by construction, dense-factor fits stuck at exactly the diagonal-only error 38.8% for 10 rounds. Sinks: any output not on the quotient (B).

C6 [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY] The teacher operator is discontinuous in geometry: +0.01% thickness -> one direction +59.8% (mu_max 1.598) via a 5.6e-15-volume cell and 3 GP faces; operator central differences at h = 1e-4 vs 1e-3 disagree by 87%; cross-seat eps_op 536-3847 at distance 0.14-0.36 (whitened Lipschitz ~1e3-1e4 at both scales). Sinks: interpolation-based generalisation at the module gate from any feasible sample count on current labels; any promise of operator-level sensitivities; any claim that 33 or 1024 seats 'cover' geometry.

C7 [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY] Hard cut classification creates discontinuities wherever it is placed: the internal-extension prototype jumps to mu_max 1.25 (3 directions > 1.1) on a 1e-12 threshold flip. Sinks: 'fix continuity with a better classifier'.

C8 [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED] Measured reachability floors: block-diagonal D 63-204x above the +-10% line (closed-form oracle); descended lifting T at 7.4M params eps_op 15.2; banded L + rank-M has lam_min(H0) = 0.02-0.13 << 0.9 so no M can pass, and hardening made it worse ([0.12, 23.6]); fixed one-layer collar mu_max >= 1.111 (Loewner). Sinks: representations (c), (d), (e) as they stand.

C9 [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED (a)] The only representation that passes +-3% needs 13.9-15.6% of dense (>= 1.2e7 numbers/cell; 11.8-13.6% for +-10%); the gate barely changes the size, so the near field dominates storage while the far field decides the verdict; approximating A instead of R* costs 1.17x more. Sinks: 'small model' claims without a computed oracle floor.

C10 [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED (a)] The H-matrix ranks were adaptive from the true blocks and SVD factors are gauge-non-unique; fixed ranks per level are untested; only block products/actions are valid labels. Sinks: coefficient regression of hierarchical factors; quoting 12.23M as a learned-model parameter count.

C11 [GOAL][REPRESENTATIONS TRIED (e)] Teacher cost 31.85 s on 64 cores per cell; collar end-to-end ~30 s (17.7 local assembly + 3.7 compile + 7.7 pre-elimination) and still needs the fine factor. Sinks: any inference path that keeps fine local assembly + pre-elimination in the loop without a 10x reduction; mode B without a cost model for the true operator's action.

C12 [GOAL] eps_op needs R* of the test geometry; only 33 seats have R*, all FULL, sparsely sampled. Sinks: held-out generalisation claims at +-10% from <= 7 held-out seats each 500-4000 eps_op from its neighbours; deployment to CUT-through-boundary cells.

C13 [ASSEMBLY / DELIVERABLE] Compliance is first order in general (dC = -u^T dK u); the 0.31% at eps_op 0.152 is construction-specific (two copies of one seat, 4 self-equilibrated end loads, weakly aligned error directions); displacement ~ eps_op/4 in that construction only. Sinks: a task-level gate without registered scope and its own multi-load, multi-assembly test suite.

C14 [ASSEMBLY / DELIVERABLE] (inference) The module gate composes by Loewner order to lattice-level energy-norm and compliance bounds (~+-eps for every load), but gives no bound on design sensitivities, which have never been tested. Sinks: assuming 'module gate passed' = 'TO-ready'.

C15 [STRUCTURE OF S][GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY] GP is what makes soft directions FP64-measurable (no-GP cond ~4e16); the same GP sets the labels' soft-direction stiffness (the 60% jump arrived with 3 new GP faces), and per-direction physical validity is unmeasured (Tet10 validates compliance only). Sinks: stabilisation changes that reopen unmeasurable directions; treating +-3% fidelity to soft directions as physical fidelity without a gamma sweep.
C16 [LEARNING ATTEMPTS] A one-sided extreme-mode term moved mu_max 15 -> 5 but mu_min 0.13 -> 0.05. Sinks: naive one-sided worst-direction losses.

C17 [LEARNING ATTEMPTS] Best neural result on any seat, train or held-out: eps_op ~ 4 (mu in [0.05, 5]); V1 mu_max 670 with train = held-out at 27% e_A, i.e. it did not memorise its own training seats in the whitened metric. Sinks: any plan that starts from generalisation rather than one-seat memorisation.
C18 [OPEN DECISIONS] Contract (module vs task) and deployment mode (A vs B) are undecided and differ by 30x in gate. Sinks: any comparison of paths before these are fixed.
open_questions: Rank 1 (cost: 2 teacher runs at gamma = 1e-3 and 1e-5 on seat 0328, ~minutes on 64 cores, + one whitened eval; impact: decisive) - Are the deciding soft directions physics or stabilisation? If eps_op between gamma-variants of the teacher exceeds 0.1, the +-3% module gate demands reproduction of an arbitrary parameter and the contract/label decision must precede any learning.

Rank 2 (cost: hours with the full-spectrum evaluator and the existing physical/fragment mode classification; impact: decisive) - Which modes decide each verdict (H-matrix 0.03, Newton 0.047, collar 0.15, the D/d 1.27e-5 case), and are they among the ~6 small-cut-fragment modes or the 188 thin-material modes? If fragment modes decide, a registered-scope gate (fragment subspace projected out or stiffness-floored) may already be passed by results in hand.

Rank 3 (cost: ~9 teacher runs along the existing +0.01% thickness path at spacings 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1, plus eps_op of the endpoint-averaged factor at each midpoint; impact: decisive) - Is the module-level map interpolable at all? Count activation events per unit thickness and the eps_op of the ideal smooth interpolant; if it fails +-10% at spacings far above any achievable sampling density, no smooth learner can pass the module gate on current labels.

Rank 4 (cost: hours-days with the 2-cell/2x2x2 harness extended to 4x4x4, Shat from the H-matrix at +-10% or a noisy factor, FD of end-load compliance along the geometry path; impact: decides the contract) - Does a +-10% module preserve TO-relevant quantities: displacement, compliance under non-self-equilibrated loads, and design sensitivities against the teacher's stable task-level derivative (0.023%)? Also measures lattice-level error accumulation beyond 2 identical cells.

Rank 5 (cost: ~1 hour, rerun the Newton+Armijo dense fit longer and with a two-sided log-symmetric extreme term; impact: high) - Is mu in [0.956, 1.047] a loss ceiling or a budget stop? If a ceiling, no gradient-trained factor through that loss can reach +-3% regardless of architecture.

Rank 6 (cost: minutes, time one PCG interior solve of 0328 and count refinement actions from eps_op 0.9; impact: decides mode B) - Does mode B's per-action cost times the iteration count beat 31.85 s per cell, given that the teacher factorises once and serves unlimited loads?

Rank 7 (cost: hours-days, one seat, unlimited steps, any representation with a computed oracle floor (scaled dense factor or fixed-rank H-blocks), worst-direction loss; impact: high) - Can a neural network memorise ONE seat to +-10% eps_op? This yields the first real network residual-noise model (entry-relative vs coherent vs soft-mode-aligned), which sets the true precision budget (currently a 100x uncertainty).

Rank 8 (cost: hours with the hierarchical builder; impact: medium) - Does an H-matrix with fixed ranks per level and a tree/admissibility transferred from another seat still pass at ~15% of dense, and are its block products continuous across nearby geometries?

Rank 9 (cost: if packets hold dense S, ~seconds-minutes per dense Cholesky at d ~ 13k; impact: medium, data-side) - Why do only 33 of 1024 packets have R*? If the bottleneck is self-imposed, 30x more whitened-evaluable labels exist for free.

Rank 10 (cost: hours with the Loewner-bound tool; impact: medium, conditional on cost) - Does a 2-layer collar clear mu_max < 1.03/1.10, and can pre-elimination be amortised or coarsened to bring the ~30 s forward map under the teacher's cost?

Rank 11 (cost: new teacher runs for two different seats sharing a face; impact: high for the deliverable) - Does assembly of HETEROGENEOUS cells (different active node sets/GP faces at the shared face) reproduce a direct solve, as the two-copies-of-0328 test did? A TO lattice is heterogeneous by definition.
Rank 12 (cost: hours; impact: medium) - What is the cheapest NON-learned approximation that passes +-10% below 31.85 s? Without this baseline the marginal value of learning is unquantified.
Rank 13 (cost: minutes; impact: low) - Is the 48-op augmentation applied consistently to the 65^3 x 11 fields, node numbering and quotient map B, and is the network equivariant or must it pay 48x?

Rank 14 (cost: analysis only; impact: low unless A is predicted directly) - Is FP32 output precision sufficient for the chosen parameterisation (fine for a factor at 1e-4 per entry; borderline for A at 4.2e-7 relative worst case)?
full_text:
# Adversarial audit of results, 2026-09-11 to 09-16

## 0. Headline

The six days characterised the target (metric, structure, geometric stability, compressibility) and produced several fits to a known label. They did not measure a learner. The best neural result on any seat, train or held-out, is eps_op ~ 4 (mu in [0.05, 5] after the extreme-mode term); plain V1 had mu_max 670 on its own training seats [LEARNING ATTEMPTS]. The work gate is 0.10. Every near-gate number in the log was produced either by consuming the true factor R* (H-matrix oracle 0.03 at 15% of dense; Newton fit 0.047 with A known) or by re-running physics per geometry at teacher-like cost (collar 0.15 at ~30 s, teacher 31.85 s) [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED]. The project narrative ("next, learn the H-matrix / dense factor / collar from geometry") steps over the one thing the log shows has never happened: a network reproducing a single labelled seat to +-10% in the whitened metric.

## 1. Hard constraints (measured; each sinks a path that ignores it)

C1 [METRIC] Worst-direction only. eps_op = max|mu-1|; 3 of 12,792 modes decided a verdict; D/d = 1.27e-5 cleared the +-3% necessary line by 36x while eps_op = 0.229 failed +-10%; the D/d floor 0.0295 corresponds to eps_op 58. Sinks: any path whose evidence or training signal is an average (Frobenius, mean divergence, e_A, action-MSE).

C2 [METRIC] Additive error on A is amplified by cond(A) = 7.2e4 (lam 4.9e-7..3.5e-2): worst-case +-3% needs ||E||_2 <= 1.46e-8, i.e. 4.2e-7 relative; even entry-relative error on A needs ~5.5e-5 [ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS]. Sinks: direct regression of S with generic residuals.

C3 [METRIC][ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS] Factor error is unamplified (eps_op ~ 1.42||Delta|| for Rhat = (I+Delta)R*), but the entry budget is still ~2.7e-4 independent / ~1.2e-4 coherent (eps_op ~ 111 x eps, i.e. ~sqrt(d) amplification, so it tightens with cell size), and 1e-3 RMS noise on a different parameterisation moved [0.863, 1.114] to [0.707, 1.377]. The noise model of a real network's residual is unknown - a 100x uncertainty in the budget. Sinks: any regression whose demonstrated relative precision is 1e-2..1e-3 (all neural results so far).

C4 [STRUCTURE OF S] Soft-direction stiffness is a near/far-field cancellation with ratio 1e3-1e4. Truncating the TRUE factor to radius 0.25 (6% of dense) gives eps_op 58; ~300 modes are damaged at every radius; mu_max stays 59-144. Consequence (inference): if the cancelling terms are predicted rather than computed, the far field needs ~1e-5 relative precision to land the soft stiffness at +-3%. Sinks: banded/local factors; bounded receptive fields (V1: 0.23); locality arguments from Frobenius energy (99.87% within 0.05 is irrelevant to the verdict).

C5 [LEARNING ATTEMPTS] Ten rounds of dense-factor + Frobenius fitting stuck at exactly the diagonal-only error 38.8%; only rigid-invariance-by-construction removed the attractor. Sinks: any output not on the quotient B.

C6 [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY] The teacher operator is discontinuous in geometry: +0.01% on all thicknesses changes ||A||_F by 2.3e-4 but one direction's stiffness by 59.8% (mu_max 1.598), through a background cell of volume fraction 5.6e-15 and 3 new GP faces; operator central differences at h = 1e-4 vs 1e-3 disagree by 87%; cross-seat eps_op is 536-3847 at geometric distance 0.14-0.36. The whitened Lipschitz constant is of order 1e3-1e4 per unit geometry at both scales. Sinks: generalisation by interpolation at the module gate from any feasible sample count on current labels; any operator-level sensitivity promise; the idea that 33 (or 1024) seats "cover" geometry.

C7 [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY] Hard classification moves the discontinuity, it does not remove it: the internal-extension prototype brought the neighbouring-geometry ratio to 1.016 but a 1e-12 threshold flip gives mu_max 1.25 with 3 directions > 1.1. Sinks: "a better classifier".

C8 [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED] Measured reachability floors: block-diagonal D is 63-204x above the +-10% necessary line (closed-form oracle); descended lifting T at 7.4M params gives eps_op 15.2 (37x worse than the unfitted H-matrix at fewer numbers); banded L + rank-512 M has lam_min(H0) = 0.02-0.13 << 0.9, so no softening term can pass and hardening made it worse ([0.12, 23.6]); fixed one-layer collar has a Loewner lower bound mu_max >= 1.111. Sinks: (c), (d), (e) as they stand.

C9 [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED (a)] The one representation that passes +-3% needs 13.9-15.6% of dense on 4 seats (12.23M numbers on 0328), 11.8-13.6% for +-10%. The gate barely changes the size: the near-field dense blocks dominate storage while the far field decides the verdict. Approximating A instead of R* costs 1.17x more. Sinks: any "small model" claim without a computed oracle floor.

C10 [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED (a)] Ranks were chosen adaptively from the true blocks; SVD factors are gauge-non-unique (signs, rotations in repeated singular subspaces). Sinks: coefficient regression of H-factors; quoting 12.23M as a learned parameter count; any fixed-rank claim (untested).

C11 [GOAL][REPRESENTATIONS TRIED (e)] The bar is 31.85 s x 64 cores per cell per geometry. The collar costs ~30 s for a new geometry (17.7 + 3.7 + 7.7 s) and still needs the fine factor. Sinks: paths that keep fine local assembly and pre-elimination in the inference loop without a 10x reduction; mode B without a cost model for the true action (an interior solve of 218,394 dofs per action).

C12 [GOAL] eps_op requires R* of the test geometry. 33 seats have R*, all FULL. Sinks: held-out claims at +-10% from <= 7 held-out seats each 500-4000 eps_op from their neighbours; deployment to CUT-through-boundary cells (no labels).

C13 [ASSEMBLY / DELIVERABLE] Compliance is first order in general (dC = -u^T dK u). The 0.31% at eps_op 0.152 came from two copies of one seat under 4 self-equilibrated end loads whose responses were weakly aligned with the error directions; displacement ~ eps_op/4 there (4.1% at 0.152, 0.94% at 0.026). Sinks: a task-level gate without a registered scope and its own multi-load, multi-assembly, sensitivity test suite.

C14 [ASSEMBLY / DELIVERABLE] (inference, not measured) eps_op <= eps means (1-eps)A <= Ahat <= (1+eps)A on the quotient; congruence and summation preserve Loewner order, so any lattice assembled from such cells satisfies (1-eps)K <= Khat <= (1+eps)K and every load case's compliance is within ~+-eps. This is why the module contract is the safe one and why 0.31% << 15% was luck. It gives no bound on derivatives. Sinks: "module gate passed = TO-ready".

C15 [STRUCTURE OF S][GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY] GP is what makes the soft directions FP64-measurable (no-GP teacher cond ~4e16, min E/N now 1.5e27), and the same GP sets their stiffness (the 60% jump arrived with 3 new GP faces). Per-direction physical validity is unmeasured: Tet10 validates assembled compliance (0.05-0.10%), an average. Sinks: stabilisation changes that reopen unmeasurable directions; reading +-3% fidelity to the teacher's soft directions as physical fidelity.

C16 [LEARNING ATTEMPTS] A one-sided extreme term moved mu_max 15 -> 5 and mu_min 0.13 -> 0.05. Sinks: naive worst-direction losses; the loss must be two-sided.

C17 [LEARNING ATTEMPTS] V1: train = held-out at 27% e_A, mu_max 670; the network did not memorise its own training seats in the whitened metric. Sinks: any plan that starts at generalisation.

C18 [OPEN DECISIONS] Contract and mode undecided; gates differ 30x. Sinks: comparing paths before deciding.

## 2. False comforts

F1 D/d, e_A, Frobenius or action-MSE improvements. Not evidence (C1). V1's "27%" is such a number.

F2 "99.87% of off-diagonal energy within 0.05" and "top-8 singular values carry >= 99.5% of far-field block energy". Energy statistics license nothing about the verdict: the true factor banded at any radius fails (C4), and the H-matrix needed adaptive ranks to pass (C10). If rank 8 sufficed everywhere the storage would be far below 15% of dense.

F3 "The H-matrix passes +-3% at 12.23M numbers". An oracle compression of a known R* on 4 seats with adaptive ranks; the fixed-rank, transferred-tree, gauge-free, learned version has not been attempted. It is an upper bound on what the representation can do, not a model size.

F4 "Column scale predictable from local geometry, R^2 0.98, LOSO curvature spread 1e4 -> 16.8". This is a preconditioner result: 0.98 in a quantity spanning decades leaves scale errors of order a factor of a few, orders of magnitude from +-3%. It licenses "the coordinates are optimisable", not "a label is predictable".

F5 "Collar + core reaches eps_op 0.15 with 23,016 params". The 6x6 tensors were optimised per geometry against the label (a fit, not a prediction); the Loewner bound proves the fixed collar cannot pass +-10%; the forward map costs as much as the teacher and still uses the fine factor. It is the strongest accuracy-per-parameter result and the weakest cost result.

F6 "Compliance error <= 0.31%". Construction-specific (C13). The Loewner bound (C14) says the guarantee at eps_op 0.152 is ~15-18%; the measured 0.31% is alignment luck.

F7 "Teacher validated against Tet10 to 0.05-0.10%". Validated at the task level. The directions that decide eps_op (stiffness 1e-6, 0.014% of mean) contribute nothing measurable to those compliances; their values are GP-dependent by construction (C15) and have never been checked against an independent reference.

F8 "Task-level derivative stable to 0.023%". One path, one 6-D end-load response, one seat; stable for the same reason F6 holds (the unstable directions barely participate). It says the teacher's dC/dtheta is a fine target; it does not say a network's dChat/dtheta = -uhat^T (dKhat/dtheta) uhat will match it, and no gate bounds that (C14).

F9 "Internal-extension GP reduces the neighbouring-geometry ratio to 1.016". The discontinuity moved to the classifier threshold (C7). Not a continuous stabilisation.

F10 "Newton + Armijo reaches mu in [0.956, 1.047] on the free dense factor". With A known, Cholesky is exact in seconds; a gradient method stopping at 5% worst-direction error after 228 steps either exhibits the loss's blindness to the last modes (then it is a ceiling for every network trained through that loss) or was stopped by budget. The log does not say which.

F11 "48 cube ops = exact augmentation". Exact within an orbit; it does not reduce the ~1e4 whitened Lipschitz constant or the 500-4000 gaps between seats, and it costs 48x training unless the network is equivariant.

F12 "V1 underfit, not overfit, so add capacity". The representation V1 emitted has a measured reachability floor (C8, lam_min(H0) 0.02-0.13). The diagnosis is confounded between representation, optimisation, loss blindness and capacity; V1 says nothing about geometry -> operator learnability.

F13 "Exact condensation composes to 1e-12". Exact algebra composes; approximate modules were composed only as two identical copies. Heterogeneous interfaces (different active node sets / GP faces on the shared face), which a TO lattice consists of, are untested even for the teacher.

F14 The tool inventory (closed-form D oracle, fixed-L reachability criterion, lifting inverse, 22x sparse gradient). Built for representations (c) and (d), both now known to be reachability-limited. The reusable tools are the full-spectrum evaluator, the assembly harness, the Loewner-bound machinery, the hierarchical builder and the teacher rebuild.

F15 "188 of the softest modes are physical thin-material modes". "Not dominated by a small cut fragment" is a support statement, not a statement that their stiffness value is GP-converged; and a 1.1e-6-stiffness direction moved 60% on a 5.6e-15-volume activation, which is either one of the ~6 fragment modes (then fragment modes decide verdicts) or evidence that the classification is incomplete.

## 3. Untested assumptions every path depends on, ranked by test cost x path impact

1. The deciding soft directions are physics, not stabilisation. Test: re-condense 0328 at gamma = eta = 1e-3 and 1e-5, whitened eps_op between the teachers. Cost: two teacher runs (~minutes on 64 cores) plus one evaluation. Impact: if eps_op > 0.1 between gamma-variants, the +-3% module gate is fidelity to an arbitrary parameter and decisions (1) and (4) must precede all learning.

2. Verdict-deciding modes are the ones TO cares about. Test: for the H-matrix (0.03), Newton (0.047), collar (0.15) and the D/d = 1.27e-5 case, list the modes with |mu-1| largest and classify them physical vs fragment with the existing tools. Cost: hours. Impact: if fragment modes decide, a registered-scope gate (fragment subspace projected out or stiffness-floored) may already be passed by results in hand.

3. The module-level map is interpolable. Test: teacher runs along the existing thickness path at spacings 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1; count activation events; eps_op of the endpoint-averaged factor at each midpoint. Cost: ~9 teacher runs. Impact: if the ideal smooth interpolant fails +-10% at spacings far above any achievable sampling density, no smooth learner can pass the module gate on current labels, which forces continuous labels or a task contract.

4. A +-10% module preserves TO-relevant quantities. Test: 4x4x4 lattice of 0328 with Shat from the +-10% H-matrix and from noisy factors; displacement, compliance under non-self-equilibrated loads, and FD end-load compliance sensitivities along the geometry path vs the teacher's stable 0.023% derivative. Cost: hours-days on the existing harness. Impact: decides the contract, measures accumulation beyond two cells, and gives the first sensitivity number.

5. The 5% Newton result is a stop, not a ceiling. Test: continue the fit; add a two-sided log-symmetric extreme term (Lanczos on the whitened operator). Cost: ~1 hour. Impact: if it is a ceiling, no gradient-trained factor through that loss reaches +-3% regardless of architecture.

6. Mode B is cheaper than the teacher. Test: time one PCG interior solve of 0328, count refinement actions from eps_op 0.9. Cost: minutes. Impact: decides deployment mode; the teacher factorises once and serves unlimited loads, so mode B likely loses unless an action is ~10 ms.

7. A network can reach 1e-4-class precision at all. Test: one seat, unlimited steps, worst-direction loss, any representation with a computed oracle floor (scaled dense factor, fixed-rank H-blocks). Cost: hours-days. Impact: first neural eps_op; first real residual-noise model (C3's 100x uncertainty).

8. A fixed-rank, transferred-tree H-matrix still passes and its block products vary continuously with geometry. Test: hierarchical builder on the 4 seats with ranks fixed at the observed maxima; nearby-geometry block-product comparison. Cost: hours. Impact: viability of (a) as a learning target.

9. Labels are limited to 33. Test: factor a 1024-batch packet (dense Cholesky at d ~ 13k is ~7e11 flop). Cost: minutes per label if S is stored densely. Impact: 30x more whitened-evaluable labels; matters only after 1-7.

10. A thicker collar is reachable and affordable. Test: 2-layer collar Loewner bound; pre-elimination amortisation. Cost: hours. Impact: revives (e) only if the ~30 s forward map drops well below the teacher.

11. Heterogeneous cells assemble exactly. Test: two different seats sharing a face vs a direct solve. Cost: new teacher runs. Impact: deliverable-level; a TO lattice is heterogeneous.

12. Learning has marginal value over a non-learned approximation. Test: cheapest non-learned +-10% method under 31.85 s. Cost: hours. Impact: sets the baseline any learned path must beat.

13. Augmentation is applied consistently to fields, numbering and B. Cheap, low impact.

14. FP32 output suffices for the chosen parameterisation. Analysis only; matters only if A is predicted directly.

## 4. Implications

Representation: factor form on the quotient; global information flow; (c), (d), one-layer (e) dead as-is; >= 1.2e7 numbers per cell with the best known structure and no smaller floor demonstrated; supervise products/actions; accuracy-per-parameter favours physics-structured forward maps, so the real open question is cost, not accuracy.

Loss and metric: two-sided worst-direction term in the whitened metric at every step; eps_op as the only gate, train seats first; resolve the Newton ceiling; gauge-free supervision; the gate is contract-dependent and neither contract has been tested on sensitivities; the metric's soft directions are GP-dependent until rank-1 is run.

Data and teacher: 33 FULL labels cannot support a held-out claim at the module gate; the 1024 packets may be factorable for free; augmentation does not help across seats; activation events make module-level labels a step function along TO paths, so the continuity decision (4) is upstream of all label generation and must preserve FP64 measurability.

Architecture: global receptive field, quotient output, variable trace dimension, equivariance; either 1e7-1e8 outputs at 1e-4 precision or physical parameters plus a differentiable assembly whose cost is the real problem; hard-classified inputs are forced by the label-continuity decision; no architecture work is warranted before a one-seat memorisation exists.

## 5. Internal tensions I could not resolve from the facts

- Only 33 of 1024 packets have R* although a dense Cholesky at d ~ 13k costs seconds to minutes: either the packets are not dense S, or the label bottleneck is self-imposed.
- "188 soft modes physical" vs a 1.1e-6 direction moving 60% on a 5.6e-15-volume activation (F15).
- V1's underfitting is attributed to the network while its representation has a measured reachability floor (F12).
- The Newton fit's 228 steps / 25 min: plateau or budget stop (F10); the two readings lead to opposite conclusions about the loss.
- The 6x6 collar tensors were optimised per geometry; whether they are smooth or learnable functions of geometry was never asked, so (e) has the same untested-learnability gap as (a).
